script.base: No spread or total was saved, so this is inferred from three weeks of form only. Both defenses have leaked: NYG allows 4.94 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, ARI allows 4.63 YPC, 11 runs of 10+, and 9.03-9.58 YPA everywhere with 9 passes of 20+. Base case is a competitive, play-filled game, not a 13-10 slog. ARI (Brissett 8 rushes, 28 yards in the log) lives through Trey McBride (34 targets, 211 yards) and a Love/Allgeier committee (41 and 24 carries). NYG hands Cam Skattebo the ball (50 carries, 177 yards) and throws to Isaiah Likely (23 targets) with unfinished verticals to Malik Nabers (96 yards on 185 air) and Malik Fields (74 on 213). NYG blitzes 26% and ARI EPA/dropback falls from +0.18 unblitzed to -0.12 when blitzed, so ARI completions stay short. ARI blitzes only 22% and NYG is +0.28 EPA when not blitzed, so NYG can run and throw.
script.flip1: ARI falls behind and abandons the run. Love's carries die toward the 29- and 41-yard rush games, McBride's 11-target floor rises, and Wilson's 295 air yards get extra chances. NYG can sit on the lead, which pushes Skattebo's carries up and shortens late pass volume.
script.flip2: NYG's soft run defense (4.94 YPC) lets Love repeat the 90-yard rush path, ARI leads and grinds, McBride's day looks like the 41-yard game, and NYG chases through Likely/Nabers/Fields while Skattebo's carries drop toward the 36-yard rush game.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. NYG did not need to blitz McBride into a 70-yard day: the middle 'bleed' was 9 throws of noise, the real pass defense held the edges at 6.7 YPA, and Brissett's -0.12 EPA vs pressure showed up as sacks instead of tight-end dumps, so McBride repeated the 41-yard game and finished under 63.5. Separately, ARI's 4.63 YPC was just the last three opponents, Skattebo stayed at 3.54, the 36-yard game was the chase script, and 60 yards lost to 62.5 with Harris vulturing the cheap yards. The coin-flip no-vig was the market saying both numbers were already right, and a 3-game heuristic was not a model.
slip_story: One story only: competitive game or NYG in front, not an ARI grind. McBride over is the ARI checkdown answer to a 26% blitz; Skattebo rush over is the NYG lead-back answer to a 4.63 YPC run defense. Those two win together in the base script and in the ARI-trails flip, and they lose together if ARI leads big and grinds. Do not add Fields, Wilson, or a total under to this slip; those need a different script. No TDs, one market per player, two legs. Fields remains a standalone safety-out note, not a ticket leg.
